label: cut button
description: I somehow landed on CUT's The Button, specifically the "gay edition." The premise is simple and brutal. Two people sit across from each other with a big red button between them. If either person presses it, the date is instantly over. No warnings. No explanations. I got so caught up in the set, the lights, and the whole surreal experience that I completely forgot the button existed. Cue me enthusiastically describing my hobbies and getting buttoned off almost immediately. Still one of the funniest "I was there for a good time, not a long time" moments of my life.

label: linkedin interview
description: A cameo on LinkedIn's 5 to 9 series, where I talk about life beyond the day job, specifically building Stellar Effects, my solo AR filter studio. What started as a side project turned into billions of impressions, six figures in revenue, and collaborations with artists and brands like Rick Astley, AJR, 5 Seconds of Summer, Connor Franta, Elle Mills, and MOD Pizza. Built after hours, powered by curiosity, and way bigger than expected.

label: greeting cards
description: An Etsy shop called Highs Lows and Rainbows that I started with one of my best friends, Anjuli. The name is a playful spin on the game Roses Buds and Thorns that we played every week during the pandemic, and it captures exactly what we wanted our cards to hold. We both love sending real mail to real people, so we started designing greeting cards that feel honest, thoughtful, and a little colorful. As the shop grew, we began turning our favorite card designs into stickers as a small extra surprise, tucking one into every order just because it felt right. What began as a crafty side project turned into hundreds of sales, all five star reviews, and a feature in Etsy's New Finds newsletter. These are our third drop cards, and they still feel like little pieces of mail we would be excited to receive ourselves.

label: floor plans
description: The floor plans of my dream home in Seattle, which I finally landed in the summer of 2025. I discovered a local builder whose Scandinavian aesthetic instantly clicked, followed along, and even sent feedback when they shared these designs. When the homes first went up for sale, I was funemployed and fully devastated. They ended up being rented out for a year, which gave me time to get back on my feet and stay in touch. As soon as the rentals ended, I submitted an offer before the home even hit the market. A four story standalone townhome built with premium materials and a lot of patience. Proof that timing, persistence, and a little manifesting go a long way.

label: slit scan
description:
I built the original Slit Scan AR filter that went viral across Instagram and TikTok. The effect captures a single vertical slice of video and maps it across time, meaning one thin column of pixels stays frozen while everything else keeps moving. The result is real time spatial distortion. Faces stretch. Rooms bend. Reality glitches.

What looks like a silly face warp is actually a time based visual trick that turns motion into geometry. I engineered it to run smoothly in a mobile AR environment, balancing frame capture, masking, and performance constraints so it felt instant and chaotic without breaking the camera pipeline.

It detonated into a full meme format. Creators used it for dance trends, reaction videos, outfit reveals, horror edits, and pure cursed content. Millions of videos later, it became one of those instantly recognizable effects that defined a moment of internet culture.

Designed, built, and launched by me. Just another example of turning experimental AR mechanics into something the entire timeline could not stop playing with.

label: cut lineup
description:
I starred in CUT's Lineup episode "Guess Which Man Makes the Most Money," filmed in Seattle. The concept is simple and mildly chaotic. Strangers rank a lineup of men by income based purely on vibes and a few rapid fire questions.

I talked about hosting potluck board game nights and choosing water as my drink of choice, which somehow translated into guesses ranging from fresh grad energy to secret tech salary. The confidence in those guesses was impressive.

It was a full day shoot, surprisingly intense, and genuinely so much fun. We even got paid to be professionally analyzed by strangers on the internet. A very entertaining social experiment and one of the more random ways I have ever spent a day in Seattle.

label: grounded
description:
The seventh evolution of Grounded, my recurring pop up home café where my living room transforms into a fully themed experience. For v6, we went full New Orleans. Chicory coffee. Fresh beignets buried in powdered sugar. Jazz in the background.

Friends show up empty handed. I handle the drinks, the food, and the tiny details. This one came with a full Pokémon inspired trading card drop because apparently hosting now includes world building.

People mingle. Refills happen. Conversations stretch. Powdered sugar ends up everywhere. Clean exits are unlikely.

Version 6. Lundi Gras energy. Depth increases with each pour.

label: top hacker
description: Featured by Major League Hacking as one of the top 50 most impactful hackers and as an organizer, mentor, and coach. I brought the hackathon scene to Missouri University of Science and Technology, founded and ran PickHacks, and built a campus wide builder community from the ground up. I led hackathons of all sizes, from dozens of students to hundreds, owning logistics, finance, development, marketing, and partnerships end to end. As an MLH coach, I helped thousands of students learn how to build, ship, and show up with confidence. A formative chapter in learning how to scale communities, empower builders, and pay it forward.

label: top creator
description: I became the top creator on Instagram after my AR filter Guess the Gibberish completely took over the internet. What started as a goofy word game turned into a global challenge that people could not stop sharing, racking up over 10 billion views over its lifetime. During this period, I was in contact with a product manager at Instagram, who told me I was the leading creator worldwide by impressions that month and that the filter helped drive a huge wave of new Instagram account signups. A strong reminder that sometimes the silliest ideas quack the loudest.

label: tour du mont blanc
description: A solo, slightly unhinged lap around the Tour du Mont Blanc after I got laid off from a startup in 2023. Most guides say 11 days. I planned for 7. I finished in 5, because apparently I had something to prove to myself. I showed up alone with a small backpack and hiking poles and walked through France, Italy, and Switzerland. I climbed ancient Roman roads, crossed high alpine passes, cut across glaciers, descended endless ski runs, scrambled ladders bolted into cliffs, and walked until my legs stopped feeling like mine. Some days I fell into step with strangers and shared meals and stories. Other days I walked completely alone, just the sound of my boots, my breath, and the trail stretching ahead. Somewhere along the way, I developed a ritual. I would haul a single can of Coke Zero up brutal climbs and save it for the summit. Cracking it open at the top of a pass felt euphoric, warm, flat, earned. This is where that addiction officially began. I moved faster than planned, slept hard, ate everything, and learned how capable I actually was when stripped down to the essentials. Exhausting, raw, and deeply grounding. One of the most formative experiences of my life and easily one of the best things I have ever done.

label: gibberish filter
description: I created the Guess the Gibberish AR filter on Instagram, the deceptively simple word game where nonsense snaps into meaning the moment you say it out loud. It was instant chaos in the best way. Within its first month, the filter pulled in billions of impressions, spreading across Stories, group chats, and timelines like a global inside joke. Celebrities, creators, and millions of people jumped in, turning it into one of the most viral AR effects of its era. The momentum led to me selling the rights to Fuck Jerry, exploding my personal Instagram from a few hundred followers to over 100,000 at @gu_christopher, and launching me into full time augmented reality creation. From there, it opened the door to building relationships with brands, creators, and companies all over the world. One filter. One idea. A very real internet butterfly effect.

label: boyfriend
description:
Chris and Will sitting in a tree, K I S S I N G (...is what child Chris would have sung on the playground).

My favorite co-conspirator in life. Somehow both the voice of reason and the reason I stay up too late laughing. Soft launch turned permanent feature.

label: awwwards honors
description: I submitted my personal website to Awwwards, a global platform where some of the internet's most creative websites are evaluated by designers, developers, and digital artists from around the world. The site itself (yes, the one you're on right now!!) is a playful recreation of a macOS desktop that opens into different parts of my life. Projects, photography, experiments, music, and a little unapologetic duck energy all living inside an operational operating system. Whether it wins anything or not, pressing submit was a small builder moment I'm proud of. UPDATE: gucduck.com received an Honorable Mention based on high scores from the user and jury vote. I didn't have an audience to ask, so every user vote had to come from someone who found the site on their own. Seeing 26 people do that felt pretty insane. Now there's a shot at "Site of the Day." Crossing our webbed feet!

description: Welcome to gucduck. Click this file to read how to navigate the site, what each app does, and a few duck puns.
